facts.fact: Email registration route POST /auth/email/register: rateLimit(register,3600s,max 10) -> validateBody(EmailCredentialsRequest) -> registerEmailUser -> audit('auth.email.register') -> issueTokens -> 201 {user,tokens}. A session is issued immediately on registration with no email verification step.
EmailCredentialsRequest: email z.string().email().max(320); password z.string().min(8).max(200). No complexity, breach-list or lockout policy.
registerEmailUser: findUserByEmail -> 409 conflict 'email_taken' if exists; argon2 hash; INSERT users(email,password_hash,display_name).
Password hashing is Argon2id via @node-rs/argon2 1.8.3 with memoryCost 19456 KiB, timeCost 2, parallelism 1; verify errors are swallowed to false.
users.email is CITEXT with a UNIQUE index (case-insensitive uniqueness); password_hash nullable for OAuth-only accounts; updated_at trigger.
Migration 0004 adds users.email_verified BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE and table auth_tokens(kind CHECK IN ('email_verify','password_reset'), token_hash UNIQUE, expires_at, consumed_at).

email_verified is NEVER read by login, requireAuth, or any authorization path; the only readers are accountRepository.ts (verification flow) — an unverified account has identical capabilities to a verified one.
facts.evidence: rg 'email_verified|emailVerified' apps/backend/src (non-test): only auth/providers/apple.ts:40,72-74, auth/providers/google.ts:54,60, auth/accountRepository.ts, auth/accountService.ts

facts.fact: Desktop exposes registration end-to-end: LoginScreen.tsx -> AuthProvider.registerEmail -> ipc.auth.registerEmail (IpcChannel.AuthRegisterEmail) -> handlers/auth.ts registerEmail -> authService.registerEmail -> backendClient POST /auth/email/register.
POST /auth/email/login: rateLimit(login,900s,max 20) -> validateBody -> authenticateEmailUser -> audit('auth.email.login') -> issueTokens -> 200 {user,tokens}.

authenticateEmailUser runs a dummy argon2 verify against a fixed digest when the email is unknown or has no password_hash (timing uniformity), then throws 401 invalid_credentials; wrong password also 401 invalid_credentials.
Failed login attempts are NOT written to audit_log: audit() is called only after authenticateEmailUser returns (throw happens first). Only successful register/login/oauth/logout events are audited.
Audit writes never fail the request (errors logged+swallowed); audit_log is append-only with user_id ON DELETE SET NULL and ip INET.

Four OAuth providers registered: google, github, microsoft, apple; each enabled only when its env credentials are present (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID+SECRET; GITHUB_CLIENT_ID+SECRET; MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID+SECRET; APPLE_CLIENT_ID+TEAM_ID+KEY_ID+PRIVATE_KEY).

A backend is running locally on 127.0.0.1:4000 (GET /health -> 200) and GET /auth/providers returns {"providers":[]} — zero OAuth providers configured on that instance. (Which build that process runs was not verified.)

RFC 8252 native flow: GET /auth/:provider/start validates redirect_uri (must be http://127.0.0.1 or localhost), state (8-256), code_challenge (20-256), code_challenge_method literal 'S256'; stores {provider, desktopRedirectUri, desktopState, codeChallenge} in Redis key oauthflow:<24-byte random> EX 600s; redirects to provider with backend callback URL.

Callback (GET and POST for Apple form_post): state is looked up then DELETED (single-use) before any exchange; provider error/no code redirects back with error; on success exchangeCode -> fetchProfile -> resolveOAuthUser -> audit -> mints one-time code (24 random bytes) in Redis oauthcode:<code> EX 120s bound to the desktop's codeChallenge; redirects to desktop loopback with code+desktopState. Exchange failures are logged server-side and returned as 'exchange_failed'.

POST /auth/token: one-time code deleted on read (single-use); PKCE check sha256Base64url(code_verifier) === payload.codeChallenge else 400 pkce_mismatch; user must still exist; issueTokens. Comparison is a plain string !== (not constant-time); pkce.ts verifyPkce (also plain ===, comment says 'constant-time-ish') is not used by the router.
Provider client secrets are used only server-side (exchangeCode posts client_secret from env); the desktop never receives provider credentials.

Apple: id_token verified with jose jwtVerify against Apple's remote JWKS (https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys), algorithms pinned ['RS256'], issuer https://appleid.apple.com, audience = APPLE_CLIENT_ID; subject required; client_secret is a 10-minute ES256 JWT signed with APPLE_PRIVATE_KEY (keyid APPLE_KEY_ID). JWKS is created lazily (no import-time I/O).
Apple fetchProfile computes identity.emailVerified but IGNORES it — passes identity.email to the profile regardless of the verified flag.

Google passes email only when email_verified is true. GitHub uses the /user profile 'email' field directly if present (no 'verified' check on that path); only the fallback /user/emails path filters primary&&verified. Microsoft uses mail ?? userPrincipalName with no verified check.

resolveOAuthUser links a NEW federated identity to an EXISTING user row whose email equals profile.email (SELECT id FROM users WHERE email=$1), with no email-verified precondition at this layer; otherwise inserts a new user; providers with no email get a synthetic '<provider>_<id>@users.neuropause.local' address. Identity link is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

Because github (profile-email path), microsoft and apple do not gate on a verified email, an OAuth identity carrying an unverified email equal to an existing account's email would be auto-linked to that account (account-linking-by-email pre-takeover class). Google is protected by its email_verified gate. Practical exploitability depends on each IdP's guarantees (GitHub public email verification, Apple always-verified relay) which were NOT verified here.

Desktop OAuth: PKCE verifier = 32 random bytes base64url (43 chars), S256 challenge; desktopState = 24 random bytes; loopback server bound to 127.0.0.1 on an OS-assigned port with a random 16-byte hex callback path, single settle, 404 for other paths; shell.openExternal to backend /auth/<provider>/start; state mismatch -> rejected; timeout config.oauthTimeoutMs; loopback closed in finally.
Desktop only offers OAuth buttons the backend reports as enabled (GET /auth/providers); on lookup failure it offers none and falls back to email (P13C F-8).

Access token: jsonwebtoken 9.0.3 HS256 with JWT_ACCESS_SECRET; claims {sub: userId, email}; issuer 'neuropause'; audience 'neuropause-desktop'; expiresIn JWT_ACCESS_TTL (default 900s = 15 min). Verify pins algorithms ['HS256'] + issuer + audience. No jti claim.
JWT_ACCESS_SECRET is required (no default) and must be >=32 chars; the server refuses to boot on invalid env. Single secret — no key id / rotation mechanism.
requireAuth: reads Authorization 'Bearer <jwt>', verifyAccessToken, sets req.userId/req.userEmail; 401 missing_token / invalid_token. It does NOT consult auth_sessions or any denylist.

No access-token revocation exists: no jti/denylist/blacklist anywhere in backend src. Consequence: after logout or a refresh_reused chain burn, an already-issued access token remains accepted until its exp (<= JWT_ACCESS_TTL, default 15 min).
facts.evidence: rg -i 'jti|denylist|blacklist|revokedAccess' apps/backend/src -> no matches; requireAuth.ts:13-27; jwt.ts:25-33

facts.fact: Refresh token: 48 random bytes base64url; only SHA-256 hex hash persisted in auth_sessions with user_agent and expires_at = now + JWT_REFRESH_TTL (default 2,592,000s = 30 days). Plaintext returned to client exactly once.

rotateTokens runs in a transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on token_hash; unknown -> 401 invalid_refresh; if revoked_at OR rotated_to already set -> revokes ALL of that user's un-revoked sessions and throws 401 refresh_reused (reuse detection burns the chain); expired -> 401 refresh_expired; else inserts new session row, marks old rotated_to=new.id and revoked_at=now(), returns new pair.

The reuse check (revoked/rotated) is evaluated BEFORE the expiry check, so replay of an expired-but-rotated token still burns the chain; replay of an expired never-rotated token returns refresh_expired without burning.
No purge/cleanup of expired or revoked auth_sessions rows exists (no DELETE FROM auth_sessions; no scheduled job).
facts.evidence: rg 'DELETE FROM auth_sessions|purge' apps/backend/src -> no matches; migrations/0001_init.sql:47 index on expires_at exists

facts.fact: Desktop refresh is single-flight (refreshInFlight) and restore is single-flight (restoreInFlight), explicitly to avoid re-POSTing a rotating token into the backend's reuse detector; restoreSession retries only me() after a successful rotation; a network error (BackendError.status===0) keeps the vault, a genuine rejection clears it.

POST /auth/logout revokes exactly ONE refresh token (UPDATE auth_sessions SET revoked_at=now() WHERE token_hash=$1 AND revoked_at IS NULL), audits 'auth.logout' with a 12-hex-char prefix of the token hash, returns 204. No authentication required beyond possession of the refresh token.
No 'logout everywhere' / revoke-all-sessions endpoint or list-sessions endpoint exists; the only whole-chain revocation is the reuse-detection side effect.
facts.evidence: rg 'revokeAll|logout.?all|sessions/revoke' apps/backend/src apps/desktop/src packages/shared/src -> no matches

facts.fact: Desktop logout: reads stored refresh token, best-effort POST /auth/logout (failure logged, not fatal), then clears in-memory access token and deletes vault.bin, sets status unauthenticated.
Opaque single-use tokens: 32 random bytes base64url, SHA-256 hex stored; TTL email_verify 24h, password_reset 1h.

requestPasswordReset lower-cases+trims the email, returns silently for unknown emails (no enumeration), invalidates prior active reset tokens, creates a token, mails '<appUrl>/auth/reset-password?token=...'. resetPassword enforces MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH 8 BEFORE consuming the token, then consumes atomically and updates the hash.
Postgres consumeToken is an atomic conditional UPDATE (token_hash AND kind AND consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now() RETURNING user_id) — cannot be redeemed twice under concurrency.
Password reset does NOT revoke existing auth_sessions for the user (updatePasswordHash only); an attacker holding a refresh token retains access after the victim resets their password.

ResetPasswordBody validates password z.string().min(1) (length policy is in the service); no max length on reset password other than the 256kb body limit. Reset/verify endpoints have no rate limit (only request-password-reset does).

facts.fact: The 'devices' module (migration 0010) is an ORG-scoped trusted-device registry (PK org_id+device_id, trust_status trusted|blocked|revoked) requiring org membership; it is not consulted by requireAuth or token issuance and is not login-device detection.

Desktop refresh token is stored as Electron safeStorage ciphertext (base64) in <userData>/vault.bin, written mode 0600 via tmp+rename; setRefreshToken REFUSES to persist when safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable() is false (never plaintext); getRefreshToken returns null when encryption unavailable; a decrypt failure clears the vault; an unreadable vault is QUARANTINED (bytes preserved) rather than reset.

Access token is held only in main-process memory (AuthService.accessToken) and never sent to the renderer; the renderer observes AuthStatus whose Session carries {user, accessTokenExpiresAt} only. backendClient is the only network path and runs in main.
Docs declare safeStorage is Keychain-backed on macOS and that Windows/Linux backends 'are weaker and will need review'. Not measured on those platforms.

Local-first mode (S17/FG-6): with no stored token, or when the backend stays unreachable after 5 retries, the desktop enters state 'local' with a device-local principal that holds NO token; RBAC dispatch gate hasActivePrincipal accepts only 'authenticated' or 'local' (deny-by-default); governed actor for local is 'local:<id>', and a cloud-authenticated id that forges the 'local:' namespace is DENIED.

rateLimit middleware: fixed window in Redis (INCR + EXPIRE) keyed 'rl:<bucket>:<req.ip>'; sets x-ratelimit-limit/remaining; 429 rate_limited over max. On Redis error it falls back to an in-process per-instance fixed window (capped 50,000 keys), sets x-ratelimit-mode: fallback, emits neuropause_ratelimit_fallback_total metric and a throttled warning (TD-3 — does not fail open).

Buckets applied: register 10/3600s; login 20/900s; password_reset 5/3600s (mounted app-level); semantic_health 30/60s. NOT rate-limited: /auth/:provider/start, /auth/:provider/callback, /auth/token, /auth/token/refresh, /auth/logout, /auth/me, /auth/verify-email, /auth/reset-password, /auth/request-verification.

Express 'trust proxy' is NOT set anywhere (no app.set(...)), so req.ip is the TCP peer address. Deployment docs and Helm/K8s manifests place an nginx ingress / TLS-terminating reverse proxy in front of the backend. Behind that proxy ALL clients share the proxy's IP: the login budget becomes 20 attempts per 15 min GLOBALLY, registration 10/hour GLOBALLY, password-reset 5/hour GLOBALLY, and audit_log.ip records the proxy address.

Redis client: ioredis 5.11.1, maxRetriesPerRequest 2, retryStrategy min(times*200, 2000)ms — a Redis outage surfaces as a thrown error to the limiter (triggering fallback) rather than hanging indefinitely.

CORS: origin allowlist regex /^http:\/\/(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost)(:\d+)?$/ only, credentials:false (cors 2.8.6). helmet() with library defaults (helmet 7.2.0). express.json limit 256kb; express.urlencoded extended:false limit 256kb (Apple form_post); /billing/webhook raw 1mb mounted before JSON parser. express-async-errors loaded first.

Because CORS allows only loopback origins and the desktop main process sends no Origin, browser-based web clients from any public origin cannot call the auth API; this is consistent with a desktop-only client model.

pino logger redacts req.headers.authorization, password, *.password, refreshToken, accessToken with '[redacted]'; pino-http logs every request except /health. The mailer additionally redacts token-bearing URLs in production because they are embedded in a string pino's redact cannot reach.

Authentication authority is the backend: tokens are minted and verified server-side with a server-held secret (HS256, iss/aud pinned); the client cannot self-issue or self-validate a session. Refresh tokens are validated against server state under row lock. Consistent with 'the client must never be the final authorization authority'.

Stale/replayed authorization is rejected at the refresh layer (rotated or revoked token -> 401 + chain burn; expired -> 401). At the access-token layer staleness is bounded only by exp (default 15 min) — no server-side check.

A network connection does not imply authorization on the desktop: local mode holds no token; cloud clients fail closed without an access token (deviceClient throws 401 not_authenticated when no token); RBAC dispatch is deny-by-default.
No AI component participates in authentication: the auth/users/middleware directories contain no LLM/AI provider calls; the only outbound HTTP is to OAuth provider endpoints.

Not PASS because: (1) zero HTTP-level tests for the OAuth endpoints and resolveOAuthUser; (2) the running local backend has 0 providers configured; (3) OAuth email auto-linking lacks a verified-email precondition for github/microsoft/apple; (4) no 'trust proxy' so per-IP brute-force limits collapse to one global bucket behind the documented nginx ingress; (5) access tokens are unrevocable for up to 15 min after logout/compromise; (6) password reset does not revoke sessions.
Route + service + argon2id + timing-uniform failure measured in code; integration test covers register/login/wrong-password/unknown-email (declared green in CI, not run here).

human_decisions_required: Does the public launch require functional email verification and password reset? If yes, a provider mailer plus mail credentials/domain are prerequisites (currently non-functional in production by construction).
Is OAuth sign-in in scope for launch (requires operator-held GOOGLE_/GITHUB_/MICROSOFT_/APPLE_* secrets) or is email/password-only acceptable? The local backend currently advertises zero providers.
Is an unverified self-declared email an acceptable human identity for the launch (email_verified is never enforced)? This bears directly on prior gate 10 HUMAN IDENTITY = NOT_ESTABLISHED.
Accept or reject the current OAuth auto-link-by-email policy for providers that do not assert a verified email.
Accept the bounded stale-authorization window (access token valid up to JWT_ACCESS_TTL=15 min after logout/reuse-burn) or require server-side access-token revocation / a shorter TTL.
Is account deletion (self-service) a launch requirement, or is the manual DSR SQL runbook acceptable? Includes the audit-retention vs erasure policy choice.
Approve the reverse-proxy trust configuration (hop count/CIDR) so per-IP rate limits and audit IPs are meaningful in the documented nginx-ingress deployment.
